subject: First-token consistency & sustained tokens/sec exemption request
messages:
From: Ivy Chen <ivy@brightretail.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@brightretail.com, sre@brightretail.com
Date: 2026-11-02T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Streaming SLA ask — first-token & sustained tokens/sec

Olga,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Two follow-ups from our platform/SRE team: Bright Retail needs clarity on streaming behavior for high-concurrency endpoints. Our product requires: a reliable first-token delivery (we measure at client SDK level) and a sustained token/sec expectation for long responses.

Specifically, our SRE target is: time-to-first-token (TTFT) at <=200ms p95 for streaming endpoints and sustained 120 tokens/sec per connection for long-running generation (90s+). If streaming can't guarantee that, we'll need to move to non-streaming endpoints where a 1s initial latency + bulk delivery is acceptable.

Can Redwood commit to these numbers, or do you have a documented carve-out / exception path for pilots? We attached a short log sample showing the variance we saw earlier (token-rate-logs-20261031.csv).

Attachments: token-rate-logs-20261031.csv (csv)

Thanks,
Ivy Chen
Principal SRE, Bright Retail

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Ivy Chen <ivy@brightretail.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, soojin.lee@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-02T11:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Streaming SLA ask — first-token & sustained tokens/sec

Ivy —

Appreciate the concrete numbers and the logs, that helps. Short answer: Redwood's standard hosted streaming SLO is optimized for low TTFT, but we don't currently guarantee 200ms p95 for every workload at scale without a scoped exception. There are a few levers we can propose for a pilot carve-out that should align with Bright Retail's targets or give a predictable fall-back.

Options we can offer for a pilot (summaries):
- Dedicated pilot pool: reserved GPU capacity for your endpoints reduces noisy-neighbor tail latency.
- Prefix/KV caching: for repeated prompt patterns we can short-circuit generation and improve TTFT.
- Token-emission smoothing + burst pool: allow short bursts above sustained rate and then smooth to a configured sustained target; helps handle initial entropy.
- Hybrid endpoint plan: streaming for interactivity with a documented TTFT window (e.g., 300ms p95) and a non-streaming fallback for large batched workloads.

If you're open, we can document a 6-week pilot carve-out: target TTFT <=300ms p95 for streaming (measured at our edge), sustained 100 tokens/sec averaged over 60s windows, and an operations dashboard feed (real-time metrics + alerting). We'll include an SLA appendix that lists monitoring expectations, test harness, and automatic roll-back conditions.

I'll loop in Karthik and Soojin for the technical validation and instrumentation checklist. If this proposal looks reasonable we can issue a scoped amendment for procurement and DocuSign the pilot terms.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Sales Engineer — Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

Ivy / Olga —

Technical notes to make the pilot concrete:

1) Measurement point: we should agree whether TTFT is measured at Bright Retail's client SDK or at Redwood's edge. For determinism we recommend edge measurement (reduces variability from client network). We'll include both in the dashboard.

2) What we can guarantee in pilot:
   - TTFT: 300ms p95 at our edge for streaming when pinned to a dedicated pilot pool (Nvidia A10x or equivalent).
   - Sustained rate: baseline 100 tokens/sec per connection averaged over a 60s sliding window; burst to 250 tokens/sec for the first 3s to allow high-entropy starts, then smoothing back to baseline.

3) Mitigations we will apply:
   - Model variant pinning (lower-latency quantized variant) for pilot endpoints.
   - Adaptive batching disabled for pinned pool (to prioritize TTFT over throughput efficiency).
   - Telemetry hooks: per-request token emission timestamps, edge-to-client latency, queue depth metrics.

4) Acceptance tests: run a 72-hour stress run with representative prompts (we'll coordinate prompt set) and produce p95 TTFT and sustained rate reports. Failure modes and thresholds will be defined in the appendix (available in the SLA-exception-summary.pdf).

If Bright Retail is OK with the 300ms/100 tokens/sec pilot carve-out and the acceptance test plan, we'll prepare the amendment language for procurement.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer

Olga / Karthik —

Thanks for the quick follow-ups and the concrete pilot scope. Bright Retail accepts a scoped pilot with the following carved terms:

- Measurement: Redwood edge metrics will be the primary measurement for TTFT, Bright Retail will collect client-side telemetry for comparison.
- Pilot SLA (6 weeks): TTFT <=300ms p95 at Redwood edge for streaming endpoints pinned to the dedicated pilot pool.
- Sustained throughput: 100 tokens/sec averaged over 60s sliding windows; burst allowance as described (250 tokens/sec first 3s).
- Instrumentation: token emission timestamps, edge latency, queue depth, and a daily summary report.
- Rollback: if p95 TTFT exceeds 400ms for two consecutive days or sustained rate drops below 70 tokens/sec for >10% of windows during the acceptance test, Bright Retail may pause traffic and revert to non-streaming endpoints.

Please proceed to prepare the amendment and DocuSign packet. Procurement will review the SLA appendix and confirm by EOD Friday.

Ivy Chen
Principal SRE, Bright Retail
